sprints.title: Photoshop Bootcamp
sprints.brief: Make editable visual messages that survive a client revision.
sprints.builds_on: Everyday image reading; no Photoshop assumed.
sprints.new_learning: Layers, selections, retouching, masks, local adjustment, editable type and output.
sprints.carry_forward: A reusable folder system, editable controls and a repair vocabulary for design work.
sprints.product: One Bootcamp evidence bundle; the independent changed brief supplies the achievement sample.
sprints.transfer: A different subject, audience and accent requirement; the teacher observes the learner selecting controls.
sprints.observation: Select the correct layer/mask and repair a spill without flattening.
sprints.conversation: Which existing control changes the requested feature while protecting the rest?
sprints.misconception: A finished-looking flattened image proves an editable workflow.
sprints.gate: Reopen the source file, identify the required control and make a small unfamiliar edit.
sprints.support: Provide labelled source layers and a short action checklist; keep the independent design decisions with the learner.
sprints.extension: Handle a second audience or output constraint with the same source file. Do not add a second full project.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Design Studio Explorer and Truck Ad
sprints.brief: Use visual metaphor, hierarchy and audience to make an advertisement communicate.
sprints.builds_on: Bootcamp layer, mask, type and export controls.
sprints.new_learning: Contrast, alignment, grouping, colour relationships, type hierarchy, metaphor and reasoned design choices.
sprints.carry_forward: A tested design system and explicit audience reasoning for original photography and campaigns.
sprints.product: Truck Ad working file plus an independently redesigned audience variant.
sprints.transfer: Change the truck audience and message; learner chooses imagery, hierarchy and type strategy without a reconstruction recipe.
sprints.observation: TA-OBS-01 or TA-OBS-02: sample a mask repair or purposeful hierarchy revision.
sprints.conversation: TA-CON-01 or TA-CON-02: explain tonal blending or defend audience/message.
sprints.misconception: A more complicated visual treatment is automatically more persuasive.
sprints.gate: A viewer identifies the intended message and the learner can justify a specific decision.
sprints.support: Offer a blank thumbnail grid and vocabulary card; do not choose the final message.
sprints.extension: Adapt the same message for a second format while preserving its hierarchy.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Original photography and a campaign image
sprints.brief: Create an original image campaign for a real school or community audience.
sprints.builds_on: Editable production and audience/design reasoning from Truck Ad.
sprints.new_learning: Capture planning, exposure/composition, lighting, image ethics and selecting original assets.
sprints.carry_forward: An original asset bank and campaign style that become the first motion sequence.
sprints.product: Original photo series, contact sheet, layered campaign image and source/consent log.
sprints.transfer: Replace the lead photograph or viewing format while preserving the intended message.
sprints.observation: Capture a deliberate framing or lighting change and explain the observed result.
sprints.conversation: What did the image include or leave out, and how did that shape the message?
sprints.misconception: Editing can rescue any capture, so exposure and framing do not matter.
sprints.gate: Produce an in-focus purposeful original asset and explain a capture/edit choice.
sprints.support: Use a small shot list and rotate camera roles; each student still captures attributable images.
sprints.extension: Create two mood interpretations while documenting the ethics of alteration.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: A message in motion
sprints.brief: Turn the original campaign into a 15–20 second motion message.
sprints.builds_on: Static campaign assets, hierarchy and file organisation.
sprints.new_learning: Time, sequence, keyframes, pacing, transitions, motion readability and delivery.
sprints.carry_forward: A reusable timeline and storyboard for sound design and later integrated production.
sprints.product: Storyboard, editable timeline, exported sequence and one independently changed pacing version.
sprints.transfer: Change sequence length and viewing format while keeping the core idea legible.
sprints.observation: Diagnose a timing or layer-order fault from the timeline.
sprints.conversation: How does a timing or movement choice change the audience’s interpretation?
sprints.misconception: More transitions always make a sequence more professional.
sprints.gate: The sequence communicates without a live explanation and can be revised from its timeline.
sprints.support: Offer a three-shot timeline and a worked example with different assets.
sprints.extension: Create an alternate pacing treatment that changes emotion without changing the message.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Sound tells the story
sprints.brief: Build a 30–45 second sound piece and score the earlier motion message.
sprints.builds_on: Motion cue sheet, sequencing, audience and production workflow.
sprints.new_learning: Recording, editing, voice/music/effects balance, acoustic space, mood and sound ethics.
sprints.carry_forward: A labelled sound library, mix session and audio choices for the collaborative campaign.
sprints.product: Original sound piece plus a scored motion revision with separate editable tracks.
sprints.transfer: Change audience or mood using existing recordings while preserving intelligibility.
sprints.observation: Set a workable recording level and repair an edit or balance problem.
sprints.conversation: Which sound relationship communicates the idea, and what would be lost if it were removed?
sprints.misconception: A louder mix is automatically clearer or more expressive.
sprints.gate: Narration remains intelligible and the learner can alter a specific sonic relationship.
sprints.support: Provide three labelled tracks and a small cue sheet; use accessible transcripts and visual meters.
sprints.extension: Create a purposeful version for a different listening environment.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Motion worlds and production choices
sprints.brief: Create a short moving scene that combines image, motion and sound; choose 2D or introductory 3D.
sprints.builds_on: Motion timeline, sound library and original photography.
sprints.new_learning: Depth, camera viewpoint, compositing, temporal continuity and choosing an efficient production method.
sprints.carry_forward: A dependable production pipeline and realistic scope for team work.
sprints.product: 8–15 second scene, editable source, sound and a method comparison.
sprints.transfer: Change viewpoint, framing or scene timing without rebuilding every asset.
sprints.observation: Trace the dependency from source asset to moving output and repair one link.
sprints.conversation: Why was this method appropriate, and what limitation did it introduce?
sprints.misconception: A polished 3D still demonstrates motion-graphics outcomes.
sprints.gate: Deliver a time-based result with an editable source and a reasoned production choice.
sprints.support: Use 2D as a complete route to the same motion outcomes; model new 3D controls before independence.
sprints.extension: Add a purposeful camera or lighting variation, not extra modelling detail.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Collaborative multimedia commission
sprints.brief: Create a small exhibition campaign combining still image, motion and sound for a named audience.
sprints.builds_on: Original campaign, time-based production, sound and realistic role planning.
sprints.new_learning: Collaborative authorship, shared specifications, asset handoff, audience testing and attributable contribution.
sprints.carry_forward: A published-format prototype and a record of decisions for the independent revision sprint.
sprints.product: Team multimedia package plus each learner’s identifiable source contribution, test and defence.
sprints.transfer: Each learner handles a changed requirement within their component and explains consequences for other media.
sprints.observation: Observe an individual integration repair and a purposeful handoff to a collaborator.
sprints.conversation: How does your contribution support the audience, and what changed because of another person’s evidence?
sprints.misconception: The group’s strongest final output proves every member has the same achievement.
sprints.gate: Every learner can show an attributable source contribution and defend a decision.
sprints.support: Reduce project scope and supply role cards; keep individual ownership and outcomes constant.
sprints.extension: Test an additional viewing context after the core package works.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Independent client change
sprints.brief: Independently adapt the campaign for a new audience, medium or communication constraint.
sprints.builds_on: Collaborative campaign and the evidence of its audience test.
sprints.new_learning: Selecting methods without a recipe, managing a client change and evaluating an integrated result.
sprints.carry_forward: A second independent sample across media for final portfolio selection.
sprints.product: Individual campaign variant containing purposeful image, moving image and sound with source files.
sprints.transfer: The sprint itself is the transfer: a new audience, reduced duration and a changed viewing context.
sprints.observation: Observe one unfamiliar repair chosen by the learner and record exactly what was independent.
sprints.conversation: What alternatives did you reject, and what evidence justifies the final compromise?
sprints.misconception: Transfer means applying more effects instead of responding to different conditions.
sprints.gate: A new constraint produces a justified adaptation across all three media.
sprints.support: Clarify the brief, chunk production and retain accommodations; do not choose the design solution.
sprints.extension: Handle an additional constraint only after the first variant meets its brief.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Portfolio and production defence
sprints.brief: Curate a multimedia portfolio that shows growth, meaning, independent control and a next pathway.
sprints.builds_on: Source files and evidence accumulated in every earlier sprint.
sprints.new_learning: Selection, refinement, accessible multimedia authorship, career fit and explaining evidence over time.
sprints.carry_forward: A personal portfolio and a specific next learning goal.
sprints.product: Individually authored portfolio with image, motion, sound, collaboration and transfer examples.
sprints.transfer: Repair or adapt a small unfamiliar sample selected to test an unresolved outcome; do not repeat a mastered unit.
sprints.observation: Observe a targeted independent repair and verify source-file ownership.
sprints.conversation: Which work best proves a particular outcome, and what is its limitation?
sprints.misconception: A portfolio is a folder containing every exercise.
sprints.gate: Every chosen work serves a stated audience and supports a defensible claim about learning.
sprints.support: Supply a simple navigation template and an evidence chooser; the learner selects and explains the work.
sprints.extension: Tailor a second portfolio view to a distinct pathway.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Shared Photoshop Bootcamp
sprints.brief: Learn editable communication tools for the Snowy Village identity and exhibition.
sprints.builds_on: Everyday communication and basic device use; no Photoshop assumed.
sprints.new_learning: The same ten-class technical Bootcamp as MM12, applied to a Grade 11 communication purpose.
sprints.carry_forward: Editable image/type controls, safe file practice and a design-process folder.
sprints.product: One Bootcamp bundle with an independent changed-message graphic.
sprints.transfer: Change audience and message in a supplied graphic using recoverable controls.
sprints.observation: Identify the intended editing target and make a controlled revision.
sprints.conversation: How does the edit help the audience understand the message?
sprints.misconception: A digital tool skill is useful without knowing the communication problem.
sprints.gate: Individually revise a graphic for a stated purpose and reopen its editable source.
sprints.support: Use the shared action demonstrations and simple audience choices; keep interpretation student-owned.
sprints.extension: Translate one graphic into a second output size.
sprints.course_thread: Introduce the village commission in the first launch; all later making must communicate to its audience.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Design Studio Explorer and village identity
sprints.brief: Design a coherent graphic identity and readable signs for a model winter village.
sprints.builds_on: Bootcamp editing, masks, live type and output.
sprints.new_learning: Design principles, colour wheel, type hierarchy, audience testing and physical/web output differences.
sprints.carry_forward: A village palette, type system, signs and image specifications for photography and model design.
sprints.product: Identity tile, two signs, web export and one independently adapted sign.
sprints.transfer: Change viewing distance or audience and redesign a sign while preserving the identity.
sprints.observation: Observe a measured readability test and a purposeful type/colour revision.
sprints.conversation: Why will this sign communicate at the actual viewing distance?
sprints.misconception: Readable on a laptop means readable on a model or exhibition sign.
sprints.gate: Use actual-size/actual-distance evidence to justify a sign revision.
sprints.support: Supply a type/palette chooser and blank layout, not a finished design.
sprints.extension: Add an accessible alternate-format sign with the same identity.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Photography for design and documentation
sprints.brief: Capture original images that explain objects, materials and making decisions.
sprints.builds_on: Village identity, shot list and output specifications.
sprints.new_learning: Digital camera care, SLR/tripod composition, lighting and file formats.
sprints.carry_forward: A baseline photo archive and repeatable capture method for the build log and exhibition.
sprints.product: Original photo set, contact sheet, settings record and one retaken image.
sprints.transfer: Photograph a different object or lighting situation while keeping the communication purpose.
sprints.observation: Each learner operates the camera and tripod safely and changes one capture variable.
sprints.conversation: Why is this capture/format suitable for documentation rather than simply attractive?
sprints.misconception: Editing a supplied photo demonstrates operating an SLR camera and tripod.
sprints.gate: Each learner supplies original capture evidence and a safe camera/tripod observation.
sprints.support: Use scheduled small-group camera rotations and a settings card; retain access arrangements.
sprints.extension: Solve a reflective or backlit-object problem after core camera evidence exists.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Digital solid models and technical drawings
sprints.brief: Design a village building that can be communicated and fabricated accurately.
sprints.builds_on: Village identity, object photos and evidence of scale/viewpoint.
sprints.new_learning: Dimensions, solid modelling, orthographic/isometric views, technical symbols and material thickness.
sprints.carry_forward: A checked digital building model and drawing set that authorise fabrication.
sprints.product: Individual digital solid model, dimensioned views, card prototype and technical explanation.
sprints.transfer: Change a building dimension or opening and update dependent views and parts.
sprints.observation: Observe an individual solid-model edit and a drawing/model consistency check.
sprints.conversation: How do these views describe the same solid, and where would a maker misread the drawing?
sprints.misconception: A perspective illustration or downloaded mesh is equivalent to an individually made digital solid model.
sprints.gate: Demonstrate editable solid construction and matching orthographic/isometric representations.
sprints.support: Start with a one-room building and a dimension template; keep model edits individual.
sprints.extension: Add a meaningful modular connection after required views and dimensions are correct.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Fabricate, test and improve
sprints.brief: Turn the checked digital model into a stable prototype using the simplest suitable tools.
sprints.builds_on: Approved solid model, drawings, scale and material assumptions.
sprints.new_learning: Tool-specific safe practice, tolerances, jigs, assembly order and life-cycle decisions.
sprints.carry_forward: Tested parts and a stable building prototype ready for light and interaction.
sprints.product: Prototype, fit-test record, revised model/drawing and material life-cycle comparison.
sprints.transfer: Resolve a changed thickness or failed joint by measuring, revising and retesting.
sprints.observation: Observe approved safe setup and a measured fit test; apply school equipment rules.
sprints.conversation: Which evidence caused the modification, and how did the alternative affect material use?
sprints.misconception: Machine precision removes the need to measure actual material and test fit.
sprints.gate: Stable, accurately represented prototype with observed safe practice and measured test evidence.
sprints.support: Provide pre-cut stock or a manual fabrication route; preserve design, measurement and evaluation demands.
sprints.extension: Improve a modular connection or reduce material use. Additional machines are optional.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Light, interaction and communication
sprints.brief: Use safe low-voltage lighting to direct attention and communicate a feature of the village.
sprints.builds_on: Stable prototype, audience identity and an access/maintenance plan.
sprints.new_learning: Simple circuit reasoning, polarity, switches, diffusion, reliability and communication through light.
sprints.carry_forward: A tested building module with serviceable lighting and a documented failure/repair.
sprints.product: Building lighting system, circuit representation, test evidence and communication explanation.
sprints.transfer: Adapt the lighting for a new viewing condition or repair a teacher-prepared safe fault.
sprints.observation: Observe safe isolation before changes and a systematic fault check.
sprints.conversation: What does the light communicate, and why is the chosen control simpler or more reliable?
sprints.misconception: More LEDs or a moving mechanism automatically communicate more effectively.
sprints.gate: A safe serviceable system performs its intended message and the learner can explain a fault test.
sprints.support: Use one approved switch/light circuit and a pictorial diagram; sophisticated electronics is optional.
sprints.extension: Add a meaningful interaction only after the core build passes its checks.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Snowy Village integration
sprints.brief: Assemble a coherent village exhibition from individually designed and tested modules.
sprints.builds_on: Village identity, photography, solid models, fabricated buildings and lighting.
sprints.new_learning: Interface agreements, group integration, audience testing, reliable setup and individual redesign.
sprints.carry_forward: A documented exhibition ready for video capture before the holiday break.
sprints.product: Village installation plus each learner’s model, drawing, build contribution and independent repair.
sprints.transfer: Change an access, placement or audience requirement and revise the individual module.
sprints.observation: Observe the learner checking one interface and correcting a mismatch safely.
sprints.conversation: How does your module fit the wider system, and what did audience evidence change?
sprints.misconception: An attractive group village replaces individual technical-design evidence.
sprints.gate: Every learner can trace their model, views, made parts, test and revision.
sprints.support: Use a common base and small modules; provide adapted access without removing individual decisions.
sprints.extension: Improve visitor accessibility or an interface after the core exhibition works.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Video the making and the message
sprints.brief: Make a 60–90 second video explaining the village’s purpose and design process.
sprints.builds_on: Exhibition, original photos, audience information and individual build evidence.
sprints.new_learning: Safe video/tripod capture, shot continuity, soundtrack, editing and compression.
sprints.carry_forward: A distributable video and editable project for the personal portfolio.
sprints.product: Video, original footage, editable timeline, audio/rights log and revised short cut.
sprints.transfer: Change audience or duration and independently re-edit a short section.
sprints.observation: Observe each learner operating the video camera/tripod and making an editing decision.
sprints.conversation: How do image order and sound explain the design process to a viewer who was not there?
sprints.misconception: A slideshow of supplied pictures demonstrates safe original video capture.
sprints.gate: Each learner has original camera/tripod evidence and can explain source-to-export decisions.
sprints.support: Use a short three-part story and common project template; retain individual capture/edit evidence.
sprints.extension: Create a purposeful alternate distribution version after the core video is complete.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Portfolio and design transfer
sprints.brief: Show the full design process and explain a realistic next pathway.
sprints.builds_on: Identity, original photographs, digital models, tested builds, lighting and video.
sprints.new_learning: Curating evidence, self-assessment against outcomes, career investigation and unfamiliar design adaptation.
sprints.carry_forward: A portable personal portfolio and an evidence-based next step.
sprints.product: Individual portfolio with models/views, original photography, process testing, graphics and video.
sprints.transfer: Adapt a small existing design to an unfamiliar dimension, audience or material constraint.
sprints.observation: Observe a chosen technical repair and verify individual camera/model evidence.
sprints.conversation: Which test changed your design, and what does your portfolio show about your current strengths?
sprints.misconception: Team photographs and a final model alone establish every learner’s design process.
sprints.gate: The portfolio links individual intention, source work, test, revision and explanation.
sprints.support: Provide a simple portfolio shell and evidence chooser; the learner chooses and explains examples.
sprints.extension: Adapt the portfolio for a specific programme or role.
sprints.review_focus: Read the independent/change evidence first; inspect selected source controls and two focal outcomes. Use other evidence when a judgment is unclear.

sprints.title: Mechanisms, evidence and power
sprints.brief: When does a face match become a defensible decision?
sprints.builds_on: Everyday experience of a digital system; no prior case knowledge assumed.
sprints.new_learning: Data versus information, inputs/process/outputs, thresholds, false matches and evidence versus assertion.
sprints.carry_forward: A mechanism diagram, a source card and a cautious claim to reuse when evaluating age assurance.
sprints.product: A school-entry face-matching analysis with a small source synthesis and independent changed-threshold response.
sprints.transfer: Change the setting from a police search to a school entrance and change the cost of a false match.
sprints.observation: Observe the learner tracing a system, checking a source or repairing a reasoning link; record only evidence relevant to a target.
sprints.conversation: What evidence supports your claim, who would disagree, and what condition would change your judgment?
sprints.mechanism: Image → numerical representation → similarity comparison → threshold → human decision; synthetic data only.
sprints.case: Clearview investigation (2021) alongside NIST demographic testing; distinguish historical case findings from current technical evaluation.
sprints.misconception: A strong opinion is sufficient without a mechanism, case evidence and a limitation.
sprints.gate: Explain the mechanism accurately, use specific evidence and respond to a changed condition.
sprints.support: Chunk source excerpts, clarify terms and model on a different example. The learner chooses assessed evidence and judgment.
sprints.extension: Introduce a credible counter-case or another context and explain whether the judgment changes.
sprints.scaffold: Worked mechanism and source card; blank structure for first synthesis; independent final selection and judgment.
sprints.review_focus: Close-read one independent response per ordinary sprint, alternating transfer/synthesis emphasis. Check the other for the selected target; sample defence during practice.

sprints.title: Age assurance and policy judgment
sprints.brief: How can a platform protect young users while limiting new data and access costs?
sprints.builds_on: Face matching, thresholds, error costs and source limitations.
sprints.new_learning: Verification, estimation and inference; policy objectives; impact versus implication; conditional judgment.
sprints.carry_forward: A comparison method that weighs effectiveness, privacy and inclusion before studying recommendation systems.
sprints.product: An age-assurance recommendation supported by mechanism comparison, source synthesis and changed-context transfer.
sprints.transfer: Move an assurance method to a support service where exclusion has different consequences.
sprints.observation: Observe the learner tracing a system, checking a source or repairing a reasoning link; record only evidence relevant to a target.
sprints.conversation: What evidence supports your claim, who would disagree, and what condition would change your judgment?
sprints.mechanism: Compare credential checks, age estimation and account/behaviour inference as different data flows.
sprints.case: Australian eSafety age-restriction guidance; use its current regulator and youth/industry-linked material, clearly identified as an Australian case.
sprints.misconception: A strong opinion is sufficient without a mechanism, case evidence and a limitation.
sprints.gate: Explain the mechanism accurately, use specific evidence and respond to a changed condition.
sprints.support: Chunk source excerpts, clarify terms and model on a different example. The learner chooses assessed evidence and judgment.
sprints.extension: Introduce a credible counter-case or another context and explain whether the judgment changes.
sprints.scaffold: Comparison table supplied; impact chains partially completed; final conditions chosen independently.
sprints.review_focus: Close-read one independent response per ordinary sprint, alternating transfer/synthesis emphasis. Check the other for the selected target; sample defence during practice.

sprints.title: Data, algorithms and recommendation
sprints.brief: Who benefits when a feed optimizes attention?
sprints.builds_on: Data collection, identities, error costs and conditional policy judgment.
sprints.new_learning: Data lifecycle, databases, algorithm components, ranking, feedback loops, scale and algorithmic dilemmas.
sprints.carry_forward: A traceable algorithm and feedback-loop model to connect with networks and later AI.
sprints.product: Paper recommender, theme synthesis and an independently redesigned ranking rule.
sprints.transfer: Change the ranking goal from engagement to discovery or public information and evaluate the resulting trade-off.
sprints.observation: Observe the learner tracing a system, checking a source or repairing a reasoning link; record only evidence relevant to a target.
sprints.conversation: What evidence supports your claim, who would disagree, and what condition would change your judgment?
sprints.mechanism: Interaction records → stored features → weighted ranking → exposure → new interaction records.
sprints.case: TikTok’s 2020 recommendation explanation as a historical provider account, compared with external regulator evidence and a current platform update before teaching.
sprints.misconception: A strong opinion is sufficient without a mechanism, case evidence and a limitation.
sprints.gate: Explain the mechanism accurately, use specific evidence and respond to a changed condition.
sprints.support: Chunk source excerpts, clarify terms and model on a different example. The learner chooses assessed evidence and judgment.
sprints.extension: Introduce a credible counter-case or another context and explain whether the judgment changes.
sprints.scaffold: Blank algorithm trace and theme headings; remove sentence stems from the transfer response.
sprints.review_focus: Close-read one independent response per ordinary sprint, alternating transfer/synthesis emphasis. Check the other for the selected target; sample defence during practice.

sprints.title: Computers, networks and privacy
sprints.brief: How can a technical failure become a public-service failure?
sprints.builds_on: Data lifecycle, algorithms and platform dependence.
sprints.new_learning: Computer components, evolution, protocols, routing, web services, security and recovery trade-offs.
sprints.carry_forward: A whole-system map with human and technical dependencies for evaluating AI and autonomous systems.
sprints.product: Network simulation, a source-based outage explanation and changed-service transfer.
sprints.transfer: Apply the mechanism to a hospital or community service with a different harm and recovery priority.
sprints.observation: Observe the learner tracing a system, checking a source or repairing a reasoning link; record only evidence relevant to a target.
sprints.conversation: What evidence supports your claim, who would disagree, and what condition would change your judgment?
sprints.mechanism: Device/application → local network → addressing/routing → service → response; authentication and backup dependencies.
sprints.case: British Library’s published review of its 2023 cyberattack, with Canadian Cyber Centre threat analysis as a comparator.
sprints.misconception: A strong opinion is sufficient without a mechanism, case evidence and a limitation.
sprints.gate: Explain the mechanism accurately, use specific evidence and respond to a changed condition.
sprints.support: Chunk source excerpts, clarify terms and model on a different example. The learner chooses assessed evidence and judgment.
sprints.extension: Introduce a credible counter-case or another context and explain whether the judgment changes.
sprints.scaffold: System icons and blank source table available; no complete model for the transfer service.
sprints.review_focus: Close-read one independent response per ordinary sprint, alternating transfer/synthesis emphasis. Check the other for the selected target; sample defence during practice.

sprints.title: AI, robots and human oversight
sprints.brief: When should a human rely on an automated recommendation or action?
sprints.builds_on: Algorithm traces, data limitations, networks and responsibility for a whole system.
sprints.new_learning: AI types and development, learning versus inference, neural-network models, sensor/action loops and oversight.
sprints.carry_forward: A technical distinction between generated content, prediction and autonomous action for media analysis.
sprints.product: Classifier/robot simulation, source synthesis and a justified oversight recommendation.
sprints.transfer: Move an automation system from a controlled warehouse to an assistive or public setting.
sprints.observation: Observe the learner tracing a system, checking a source or repairing a reasoning link; record only evidence relevant to a target.
sprints.conversation: What evidence supports your claim, who would disagree, and what condition would change your judgment?
sprints.mechanism: Training data and error feedback versus inference; sensor → decision → actuator with an override/stop boundary.
sprints.case: NHTSA automated-vehicle guidance and UNESCO education guidance as contrasting contexts; refresh named deployment examples before teaching.
sprints.misconception: A strong opinion is sufficient without a mechanism, case evidence and a limitation.
sprints.gate: Explain the mechanism accurately, use specific evidence and respond to a changed condition.
sprints.support: Chunk source excerpts, clarify terms and model on a different example. The learner chooses assessed evidence and judgment.
sprints.extension: Introduce a credible counter-case or another context and explain whether the judgment changes.
sprints.scaffold: Simulation structure supplied; students construct causal chains and oversight conditions independently.
sprints.review_focus: Close-read one independent response per ordinary sprint, alternating transfer/synthesis emphasis. Check the other for the selected target; sample defence during practice.

sprints.title: Media, culture and political participation
sprints.brief: Who should decide what remains visible on a platform?
sprints.builds_on: Recommendation incentives, AI-generated content, evidence limits and human oversight.
sprints.new_learning: Media forms/convergence, immersive media, source authenticity, policy enforcement and synthesis by theme.
sprints.carry_forward: A stronger method for weighing values and unequal consequences in environmental/infrastructure decisions.

profiles.title: Graphic design and image manipulation
profiles.why: The preferred starting point. Build on editable Photoshop foundations and teach the design decisions that make an image communicate.
profiles.target: A purposeful advertisement and an independently adapted audience/format version, with the editable source and a short defence.
content: Audience and purpose; visual hierarchy; type relationships; colour and contrast; image credibility and compositing decisions.
Demonstrate the actual editing controls with genuine action/checkpoint screenshots, then let students choose and defend a different solution.
Use Explorer to teach design principles before the selected guided Truck Ad work. The changed brief tests decisions beyond tutorial copying.
criteria: Audience and message
The main idea and reading order are clear for the stated audience; image/type choices support that purpose.
Explorer comparison and audience test; independent changed-audience version.
Point to the choice that matters most for this audience. What did you change after testing?
Editable image construction
The source file retains purposeful controls, and the learner can use the relevant layer/mask/adjustment to make a changed edit.
Guided Truck Ad techniques; independent revision using the learner’s own file.
Observe a targeted repair. Ask why this control protects the rest of the image.
Design reasoning and revision
The learner explains a visible design problem, the revision made and the resulting communication improvement.
Critique practice, before/after comparison and final defence.
What evidence shows that the revision improved the message?
profiles.scope: Draft criterion design for MM12 image/design outcomes. Formal descriptors, exact outcome links and approved rubric IDs must be resolved from the existing project rubric/registry. COM11 uses its village-identity task and course outcomes; it does not automatically inherit the full Truck assessment.
build: Reuse the approved Truck Ad HTML, assets and valid assessment components.
Complete Explorer teaching examples, one short practice task and a changed-audience brief.
Create a criterion-by-lesson map, sampled O/C cards, bounded reflection and an exportable versioned rubric.
profiles.handover: Use the campaign brief and design vocabulary to plan original photographs in Sprint 3.

profiles.title: Photography supplies original material
profiles.why: Photography extends the design work: students deliberately capture the images their message needs.
profiles.target: Original photographs/contact sheet, chosen image and layered campaign, source/consent notes, and an independently changed format.
content: Camera care, stable capture, focus/exposure, framing, available light and practical file management.
Use controlled comparisons: one deliberate change, a predicted result, an actual photograph, then a decision.
Teach image context/ethics and purposeful selection before applying reversible edits and design principles.
criteria: Purposeful capture and selection
The learner produces and selects an original usable image, with a defensible framing/light choice for the brief.
Capture stations and paired light studies; original shoot/reshoot and contact sheet.
Observe one deliberate capture change and ask the learner to explain the result.
Image construction and communication
The edited campaign communicates the intended idea and preserves an editable source for the new format.
Selection/edit demonstration, audience test and independent format adaptation.
Which edit strengthened the message, and where could editing become misleading?
Production decisions
The learner can trace source, capture, selection, revision and output choices using actual files.
Shot plan, source log, review and defence.
Ask for the file or comparison that supports one decision.
profiles.scope: MM12 judges the image-production/design outcomes selected for the task. COM11 Sprint 3 needs a separate course configuration addressing camera care, SLR/tripod technique, lighting and file formats; reuse instruction where appropriate, not the same outcome labels.

profiles.title: Animation makes the design work in time

profiles.target: A 15–20 second motion message, timed storyboard, editable timeline and independently changed pacing/format version.
content: Sequence, holds, keyframes, interpolation/easing, transitions, visual continuity and text reading time.

profiles.target: A mechanism explanation, small source synthesis and independent changed-context judgment, followed by a short defence.
content: Explain a face-matching system using a simplified synthetic model: inputs, representation/comparison, threshold and decision; state what the model leaves out.
Use the source pack to distinguish observed findings, claims, assumptions and limits. Teach stakeholders and selected 3Cs as analytical tools.
Move from impact to implication, then counter-perspective, trade-off and a qualified judgment under changed conditions.
criteria: Mechanism accuracy
The explanation connects the relevant system stages and shows how a changed rule can affect a decision.
Worked diagram and threshold lab; independent changed-system explanation.
Where does the decision happen, and what changes if this threshold changes?
Evidence and source reasoning
The learner uses relevant evidence and identifies a limitation affecting what can be concluded.
Source-card practice and theme comparison; independent synthesis.
Which source supports this claim, and what does it not establish?
Analysis and qualified judgment
The learner connects mechanisms to stakeholder consequences, weighs a credible alternative and explains a condition on the conclusion.
Model on another case; guided analysis; unfamiliar transfer and defence.
Who has the strongest counterargument, and what evidence would change your conclusion?
profiles.scope: These are proposed local formative reasoning criteria, not official IB markbands, IA criteria or a predicted grade. Formal Paper 1, Paper 2 and IA tasks require their current applicable assessment instruments and teacher guidance.
build: Check the historical case and current technical sources, select short purposeful excerpts and write teacher source notes.
Create the synthetic threshold lab, mechanism diagram, contrasting practice responses and source-synthesis activity.
Write the independent changed-context task, local formative descriptors and sampled defence prompts; keep teacher answers separate.
profiles.handover: Reuse the mechanism/source/qualified-claim habits when evaluating age assurance in Sprint 2.
